subject: The Papyrus · Sunrise on the shortest day: 21 December at Karnak
html:
Sunrise on the shortest day

On 21 December, the winter solstice, the sun rises in line with the walls of Karnak Temple in Luxor, and visitors gather at dawn to watch it. That is how Africanews, reporting with AP, described the morning in 2025. (Source: Africanews with AP, 22 Dec 2025.) It is not a public holiday, so shops, banks and the other sites keep their normal hours.

The morning, by the clock

EgyBI computes the sun for each site with NOAA’s solar equations. At Karnak on 21 December 2026 the sun rises at 06:31, the low golden light lasts until about 07:05, and it sets at 17:03, Cairo time. The temple opens at 06:00, with last entry at 16:00, so you can be inside before the sun comes up. (Hours: the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities booking site, checked 17 November 2026.) An adult foreign visitor pays 600 EGP on the Ministry’s price list of 5 November 2024.

Dress for the dawn, not the afternoon

December is Luxor’s kindest month to walk in: a normal afternoon at Karnak reaches about 23.5 °C, but a normal night drops to about 8.5 °C, and that cold is what you stand in at sunrise. (NASA POWER climate normals, 2001–2020.)

The same morning in Fayoum

Travel sites describe a second alignment on the same day at Qasr Qarun, a Ptolemaic temple in Fayoum; one of them gives about 25 minutes of light in the sanctuary. That comes from travel sites rather than an official page, so take it as a reason to go and check, not a timetable. (Source: Explore Fayoum.)

Put Karnak in the trip planner with your dates, and its day-by-day sheet shows the sunrise, the golden light, the opening hours and the solstice for each day you are there. The heat for every month is on Karnak’s page.
